messages:
Jules (CSM): Quick weekly check-in for EchoHealth (acct EH-231). Top highlights: hosted spend at $42.3k this billing week vs $50k commit — overall under commit, but we have 2 anomaly flags from spend-bot. See summary: https://console.redwood.ai/billing/EH-231 (link)
spend-bot: ALERT: short-term burst detected (3x baseline) between 03/14 14:10–14:26 UTC. Top contributing route: /v1/chat/stream (approx 68% of burst)
Jules (CSM): Flag details: 1) transient burst (~16m) 2) higher streaming token churn -> billed tokens up 2.8x during window 3) no obvious new seats on the account. Attached snapshot from billing dashboard shows per-route breakdown.
Ari (SRE): Can you paste the route + model combo? need to check whether batching/kv cache settings were bypassed.
Jules (CSM): Route = customer-chat-prod, model = redwood/fast-chat-8k (pinned). Request patterns show many short-lived streams that reopened quickly.
Marco (CS Ops): Noted. Any latency or error spikes during that window? That can hint at retry storms.
spend-bot: METRICS: avg latency +9ms, http 5xx rate unchanged, client-side retry count +210% for that route.
Priya (Billing): From billing side, the burst caused a mid-cycle bump but still under commit. Recommend we 1) alert EchoHealth about unexpected token churn, 2) offer quick config change (enable prefix caching + increase keepalive), 3) propose a 10% temporary top-up credit if we find product issue.
Ari (SRE): Quick triage plan: I can pull sample request headers and idempotency keys from logs (will need Marco's help to map request IDs to user sessions). Also want to check whether `stream: true` clients were reinitializing on socket timeouts.
Marco (CS Ops): I'll grep logs for repeated session opens from same client IPs and check websocket close codes.
Jules (CSM): Customer touch plan: I'll send a short note asking if they rolled out a client change 03/14. If no response in 6h, we schedule a call. Draft message: "Hi Lena — we noticed a short burst of streaming requests on 3/14 that spiked billed tokens. Can you confirm any client-side changes? We have a few mitigations to suggest."
Ari (SRE): If it's client-driven, mitigation = advise prefix caching and increasing socket timeout to avoid reconnect churn. If server side, we prepare a rollback and enable fallback to a smaller sequence-length profile.
Priya (Billing): Also flagging renewal risk: this is marginal right now but if bursts repeat we escalate to AM. I can draft a one-pager showing cost drivers and our recommended ops changes for the AM > CSM handoff.
Jules (CSM): Action items: 1) Ari + Marco dig logs (ETA 2h) 2) Jules message to customer (sent) 3) Priya prepare billing note (ETA EOD) 4) follow-up sync if customer confirms change. I'll update this thread with any replies from EchoHealth.
Marco (CS Ops): Started log pull — will post sample ids here when available.
Ari (SRE): pulled sample -> suspect repeated short streams with no KV reuse. Posting snippet:
```
{"req_id":"r-9a7b","path":"/v1/chat/stream","model":"redwood/fast-chat-8k","stream":true,"session_open":1}
{"req_id":"r-9a7c","path":"/v1/chat/stream","session_open":1}
```
Ari (SRE): Looks like clients reopened sessions quickly instead of resuming. If EchoHealth confirms a client patch, recommend client-side fix + our docs link: https://docs.redwood.ai/best-practices/streaming
Jules (CSM): Customer replied: "we rolled an SDK update around 03/14 but didn't anticipate reconnect behavior." I scheduled a short demo tomorrow to walk them thru keepalive and caching.
Priya (Billing): I'll draft the cost breakdown and include a one-off courtesy credit for noise if the SDK change caused it. Will loop AM if pattern repeats.
Jules (CSM): Thanks team — closing this check-in for now. Will re-open if we see repeat flags. :white_check_mark:
